analysis.title: US Midterm Elections and Japanese Stocks
key_insights: With 12 days to the November 3 US midterms, Daiwa AM's chief strategist Kazunori Tatebe says the direction of the stock market is unchanged regardless of the outcome, though scenario-specific impacts deserve attention.
All 435 House seats and 35 of 100 Senate seats are up. Republicans currently hold the House 219-214 (2 vacancies) and the Senate 53-47, and the US has a unified Republican government.

Polymarket (as of October 21) puts the probability of a Democratic House majority at 92% and a Democratic Senate majority at 67%. The report treats the Senate as virtually a toss-up because of multiple battleground states and doubts about polling accuracy.

Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats to reach 51, because the Republican Vice President breaks 50-50 ties. Of seats not up for election, Republicans hold 31 and Democrats 34. Republicans need 19 of the contested seats, or Democrats need 17 or more.
The ruling party has lost House seats in 20 of the past 22 elections since 1938. The protracted war in Iran and higher energy prices may add headwinds for the Republicans under President Trump.

A divided government is highly likely. Policy progress is expected to stall, but gridlock does not mean a stagnant market, since lower odds of major policy shifts raise predictability. Some analyses show higher stock returns under divided governments than unified ones.
New massive fiscal packages would be hard to pass even under unified government, given swelling US debt and high long-term interest rates.

Investors are likely to take more risk once the event passes, and stocks tend to perform strongly in the third year of a presidential term. The report calls this only a historical pattern and says macro and micro drivers matter more: the Middle East, high crude oil prices, interest rate trends, AI expectations and concerns, and corporate earnings.

Scenario 1 (Republicans win both chambers, unlikely): the status quo continues and the market reacts positively. Expectations of added fiscal spending are a tailwind, but the bond market could react with rising interest rates.

Scenario 2 (Republican Senate, Democratic House): policy stalls and stocks are likely to rise after the election. Fiscal expansion is curbed, so interest rate hikes are expected to be more contained than under unified government. Debt ceiling turmoil is a risk, and the new Congress convenes in January 2027.

Scenario 3 (Democrats win both chambers): practical outcomes are similar to Scenario 2 because bills need the president's signature. Senate control would give Democrats influence over cabinet and Federal Reserve Board governor confirmations, with a possible monetary policy impact.

Under Scenario 3, Democratic bargaining power would strengthen, especially after a landslide. A growing push within the Democratic Party to tighten regulation of AI development and data center construction could add headwinds for AI stocks, which already face heightened concerns.

AI regulation criticism is bipartisan, so the discussion proceeds under any scenario. Because the Trump administration promotes AI and stays in power until January 2029, Daiwa AM sees sweeping federal regulation as unlikely and expects any negative reaction in AI stocks to be short-lived.
Scenario 3 is the least likely of the three to push stocks higher in the short term, partly because Democrats could negotiate higher healthcare spending that shifts fiscal policy toward expansion.
Scenario 4 (Republican House, Democratic Senate) is considered highly unlikely.
A chart of TOPIX performance around US midterms from 1974 to 2022 is titled as showing TOPIX tends to rise from the midterms into the third presidential year.

sector_views.rationale: A Democratic-controlled Congress could add regulatory headwinds for AI and data center build-out, but federal regulation is unlikely under the Trump administration, so any negative reaction is expected to be short-lived.
TOPIX historically tends to rise from US midterms into the third presidential year, and the market direction is seen as unchanged by the election result.

tension_points.bull_case: Federal regulation capable of derailing AI investment is unlikely because the Trump administration backs AI and data center build-out through January 2029, and excessive regulation would undermine US competitiveness, so any negative reaction should be short-lived.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic-controlled Congress, especially after a landslide, could gain bargaining power, and the Democratic Party has a growing movement to tighten regulation of AI development and data centers, adding headwinds to AI stocks already facing heightened concerns.

theme_stances.key_argument: A divided government is highly likely and is unlikely to significantly alter the stock market's trajectory, with investors taking more risk after the event.
theme_stances.evidence: unlikely to significantly alter the stock market’s trajectory

theme_stances.key_argument: Democratic control could create short-lived headwinds for AI stocks, but sweeping federal regulation is unlikely under the Trump administration.
theme_stances.evidence: any negative reaction toward AI-related stocks will be short-lived
